exam.title: SnowPro Specialty: Gen AI
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal certification prerequisite is published. Snowflake recommends one or more years of enterprise Gen AI experience with Snowflake and assumes Python, data-engineering and SQL knowledge. Build evaluated, governed Cortex AI function, RAG/semantic/agent, open-model Model Registry/SPCS and document-processing pipelines with least privilege, versioned evidence, bounded cost and tested failure/rollback.

review.notes: All four live public abilities are mapped through use-case/data/action contracts, least privilege and responsible threats, layered retrieval/generation/tool/system evaluation, canonical Cortex AI functions and governed RAG/semantic/agent/MCP behavior, reproducible open-model Model Registry/SPCS lifecycle, and idempotent evaluated document parsing/extraction pipelines. Candidates must reconcile the form-delivered detailed guide; inaccessible weights/subobjectives are not reconstructed. Three scenarios, eight labs and 40 checks are included. All 11 links are reachable. No recalled/live item, dump or copied course content is used.

findings.title: Public abilities remain unchanged and Python is optional profile wording
The PDF content is newer than its URL filename
Caller source-table restrictions do not automatically restrict Search
API identity may differ from an active SQL session role
Default tool behavior differs from generic overview shorthand
Secure metadata does not grant data isolation
The transition recommendation is not an API retirement
Successful query execution can include failed document rows
New parsing work needs the canonical API contract
Table/list scores do not certify individual cells
No extra score charge does not make extraction free
New evaluation is preview and needs validated labels
UI model visibility differs from supported API and inference privileges
Finite jobs do not inherit long-running restart semantics
A narrow permission change can leave broad function access

local_validation.execution_boundary: Actual standard-library in-memorySQLite controlled publication/access/cache/citation and synthetic score fixtures. NoSnowflake,LLM,parser,search,embeddings,network,credentials orcloudworkload.

limitations: Only four public abilities are mapped; the detailed guide remains form-restricted. The actual five-page training PDF supports learning, not exam weights or duration.
Eight cloud labs and three scenarios remain proposed; independent human review is pending. No Snowflake SQL/API, model, parser, Search, container or GPU lab was executed.

The 43 Python/SQLite checks use one connection, controlled fixtures, trusted callers and a fixed manually ranked query. They do not test authentication, approval, concurrency, crash durability, distributed caches or external effects; SQLite key enforcement differs from standard Snowflake tables.

Citation checks verify current access and provenance, not semantic entailment. Opaque hostile text does not test model resistance to injection. Four invented extraction fixtures illustrate gate errors, not production quality.

Search service access, actual agent identity and serving version need account verification. Client filters alone are insufficient; agent prechecks do not cover every tool or underlying data permission.

Per-source notes distinguish selected sections from complete main pages. The entire linked documentation catalog was not audited. Phased bundle, preview and notebook notices do not prove account availability.

Two Udemy pages returned HTTP 403; old revision and duration metadata is unverified. Public training metadata and the PDF do not establish paid lesson quality. No forms, questions, enrollment or trial accounts were accessed.
The five reserved GitHub guides and disabled notification pilot remain untouched. No external messages, service/authentication/logging/alert changes or new permissions occurred.
